headline: CATTLE JUMP ON FEEDER STRENGTH AS CORN SLIPS BACK
lead: Live cattle are trading at $221.23 overnight, up 1.8%, with feeders up 2.0% to $340.50, both printing well above Tuesday's settle with no fresh Cattle on Feed data behind it. Corn slipped back to $5.04, giving up the round number it just reclaimed Monday as rain-stalled harvest meets heavy Grain Stocks.
teaser: Cattle and feeders both jump overnight while corn gives back the $5 handle it just won.

one_number.unit: metric tons of promised beef imports
one_number.context: Trump's 100,000 metric ton beef import plan did not show up in September trade data, and retail beef prices didn't move either.

sections.title: Cattle And Feeders Both Jump
sections.body:
- Live cattle are at **$221.23** overnight, up 1.8% from Tuesday's $217.25 settle, with feeders up 2.0% to $340.50 from $333.85.
- No Cattle on Feed report today to explain it, the move is coming from the cash side with the Cargill lockout still pulling roughly 6,000 head a day of capacity.
sections.so_what: Tight supply story just got another data point confirming it, not fixing it.

sections.title: Corn Slips Back Under $5.08
sections.body:
- Corn is trading at $5.04 overnight, down seven and a half cents from Tuesday's $5.08 close, after Monday's heavy Grain Stocks print already had the market digesting a bigger carryout.
- AgWeb's dispatch from Illinois today is the same story playing out across the Belt: combines parked, mud instead of harvest, drag-day after drag-day.
sections.so_what: Wet fields are backing up corn supply even as the stocks number argued otherwise.

outside_the_pit.title: Trump Signs Dyed-Diesel Tax Deferral Order
outside_the_pit.body: Monday's executive order defers dyed-diesel tax payments and offers penalty relief, a direct input-cost break for fall fieldwork and grain drying.

watch_list.desc: Export sales; soybeans over 1.5 MMT keeps the China-purchase story alive into harvest.
Corn above $5.08 again reopens the round-number story; below $5.00 says harvest supply is winning.
Watch feeder cash trade for follow-through above $340.50 or a fade back toward $334.
